note: Langfuse research session: Open source LLM engineering platform (YC W23, MIT licensed). Core stack: Next.js/React frontend, Node.js worker, PostgreSQL + ClickHouse (analytics), deployed via Docker/Kubernetes. SDKs for Python and JS/TS. Key integrations: OpenAI, LangChain, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM, Vercel AI SDK, Haystack. OpenTelemetry-based for reduced vendor lock-in. ~16k GitHub stars. Self-hostable in minutes via docker compose.

OpenClaw research: Personal AI assistant platform (MIT, Node.js/TypeScript) with a local Gateway WebSocket control plane (default port 18789). Connects to 20+ messaging channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal, iMessage, etc.). Supports multi-agent routing, cron jobs, voice wake, sub-agents, skills platform, and 100+ LLM models via direct or LiteLLM proxy. openclaw-dashboard is a companion Go binary (zero-dep) that provides a single-page observability UI for the OpenClaw Gateway — 12 panels covering costs, cron, sessions, sub-agents, system metrics. Pure HTML/CSS/JS frontend, no build step, stale-while-revalidate data layer.

OpenRouter scout-agent model research (April 2026): Verified live pricing — Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite: $0.10/$0.40 (1M ctx, fastest, lowest cost, tool call error rate ~6-18% is notable); Qwen3 30B A3B: $0.08/$0.28 (41K ctx default/131K with YaRN, best price-perf sweet spot, MoE 3.3B active); Qwen3 8B: $0.05/$0.40 (40K ctx, cheapest non-free); Qwen3 Coder 480B A35B: $0.22/$1.00 (262K ctx, #1 coding model by usage, best for code understanding); DeepSeek V3.2: $0.26/$0.38 (164K ctx, lowest output cost at scale, near-GPT4 quality, tool call error <1%); Gemini 2.5 Flash: $0.30/$2.50 (1M ctx, strong reasoning but 6x more expensive output than V3.2). Note: deepseek/deepseek-v3 and deepseek/deepseek-v3-0324 are no longer available on OpenRouter as of April 2026. Qwen3.6 Plus has a free tier. Key tradeoff: Qwen3 30B A3B has 41K default context limit which may be tight for large codebases — check YaRN routing. DeepSeek V3.2 has lowest tool call error rate (~0.8%) which matters for agentic use.

For simple latest-version lookups, Serper snippets can be sufficient when web_fetch is unavailable due to missing Chromium; note the fetch limitation explicitly and prefer official python.org search results.
Official python.org download page snippets expose the current latest Python version directly in search results, which is enough for concise version-only answers when fetch tooling is unavailable.
For repeated simple version queries, a single official search result from python.org is sufficient; avoid extra fetches when the result snippet already states the version clearly.

GitHub page and raw/API fetches are currently blocked in this environment because web_fetch requires Chromium; when that fails, rely on search snippets and clearly label repository-level details as unverified unless another accessible source mirrors them.

Speaker diarization research on this machine is constrained by missing Chromium for web_fetch; for documentation-heavy tasks I had to rely on official search-result snippets and clearly mark repository/detail claims as lower confidence unless corroborated by authoritative result text.

For sherpa-onnx research, official search snippets expose useful concrete details even without fetch: docs/FAQ mention `extractor.compute(stream, false)` for speaker ID; GitHub search results confirm C examples (`speaker-identification-c-api.c`) and recent releases added Rust APIs for speaker embedding extractor/manager and speaker diarization.

Verified that there are now published Rust crates for sherpa-onnx on crates.io (`sherpa-onnx` and legacy/forked `sherpa-rs` variants). The original `thewh1teagle/sherpa-rs` repo is marked deprecated because upstream sherpa-onnx now provides an official Rust API.

Wazuh current docs confirm the classic /vulnerability API exists across 4.x but is explicitly deprecated since 4.7; RBAC reference is the most reliable source for endpoint families (rootcheck, sca, syscheck, mitre, active-response) and auth docs confirm JWT via POST /security/user/authenticate?raw=true with default 900s lifetime.
